title: Independence of Several Events
short: A, B and C are independent when every pair and the triple multiply; disjoint events with positive probabilities are never independent.
trouble: Students treat mutually exclusive events as independent, though knowing one happened rules out the other. Others check only pairs: for two coin flips, "first is heads," "second is heads" and "the flips match" are independent in pairs but not all three together.

blocks.html: Two events are independent when knowing one happened does not change the chance of the other: $P(A \cap B) = P(A)P(B)$, as in independent events. For three or more events, and for events that cannot happen together, the details matter.

$A$, $B$, $C$ are (mutually) independent when all four equations hold: $P(A \cap B) = P(A)P(B)$, $P(A \cap C) = P(A)P(C)$, $P(B \cap C) = P(B)P(C)$ and $P(A \cap B \cap C) = P(A)P(B)P(C)$. Disjoint events with positive probabilities are never independent.

Independence means information about some of the events tells you nothing about the others. If A and B are disjoint and $P(A) > 0$, then learning A happened tells you B did not happen: $P(B \mid A) = 0 \ne P(B)$. Using the definition of conditioning, $P(A \cap B) = 0 < P(A)P(B)$. Pairs are not enough for three events: the triple equation says that knowing both A and B tells you nothing about C, and that is a separate fact.

blocks.name: prob-square
blocks.cap: Disjoint events: no overlap, so the joint probability is 0 while the product of the probabilities is not.

blocks.name: prob-square
blocks.cap: Two coin flips: A is first flip heads, B is second flip heads, C is the flips match. Every pair multiplies, but knowing A and B makes C certain.

blocks.title: Disjoint is dependent
blocks.q: A die is rolled. A = "roll a 1", B = "roll a 6". Are A and B independent?
steps: $P(A \cap B) = 0$, since one roll cannot be both.
blocks.a: No. They are mutually exclusive, which makes them dependent.

blocks.title: At least one of three
blocks.q: Three independent alarms sound in a fire with probabilities $0.9$, $0.8$ and $0.7$. Find the probability that at least one sounds.
steps: Complement: all three fail. By independence, $$P(\text{none}) = 0.1 \times 0.2 \times 0.3 = 0.006$$

blocks.title: Independent in pairs only
blocks.q: Flip two fair coins. A = first is heads, B = second is heads, C = the flips match. Check pairwise and mutual independence.
steps: Each event has probability $\frac{1}{2}$. $A \cap B = \{HH\}$, $A \cap C = \{HH\}$, $B \cap C = \{HH\}$: each has probability $\frac{1}{4} = \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{2}$. So every pair is independent.
blocks.a: Independent in pairs, but not mutually independent: knowing A and B forces C.

blocks.html: Treating mutually exclusive events as independent ("they have nothing to do with each other"). Exclusive events are strongly linked: one rules out the other. The second slip is checking only pairs of events. Check: for three events write down all four products, including the triple one.
